primary_coaching_focus.topic: button-up completeness on a won call
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Yeah. I see. Cool, man. Well, I'll send you that paper as soon as I get to it, and I'll, put you down for tennis, Friday.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The appointment is real and the customer is cooperative, but the rep never runs the full button-up (hour block, is-that-fair handshake, explicit reconfirmation) — on an easy, warm call this is the cheapest place to build a repeatable habit before it costs a harder call.

key_moments.quote: I had here you were the homeowner. Was it you and your wife?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep proactively surfaces co-ownership during verify, which is good practice, but never follows up later to explicitly confirm the wife will be present at the in-person Friday visit. Because this is an in-person appointment rather than a phone appointment, her absence is unconfirmed rather than a confirmed exclusion — a softer gap than a phone-appointment spouse exclusion.

key_moments.quote: I know you you might not know, but do you have any idea of, like, an average price you guys are normally paying every month? No idea, bro.
key_moments.stewart_read: Bill amount was not captured — customer has no idea what he pays. Rep acknowledges and moves on without attempting any alternative anchor (e.g., asking about kWh usage habits, AC use, home size) that could still create bill-pain framing.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. It might not be for a little while. She just opened her own, retail business, but she's over there right now.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a scheduling/logistics anchor (wife busy at her new business) that the rep could reflect back to set a soft deadline or check-in point; instead the rep simply accepts the delay and moves to confirming the phone number for texting.
